cards.text: Isaiah, a prophet, has a message, and this one covers the WHOLE earth. Isaiah says, "Behold, the LORD lays waste the earth and leaves it in ruins." He'll twist its surface and scatter its inhabitants.

cards.question: As the LORD scatters the earth's people, Isaiah names priest and people, master and servant, lender and borrower. How does the scattering fall on them?

answers.text: On every one of them alike
On the servants more than the masters
On the borrowers but not the lenders

cards.text: The earth will be utterly laid waste and thoroughly plundered. This part is heavy, friend.

cards.question: Isaiah says the earth will be utterly laid waste and thoroughly plundered. True or false: He says this is only his own guess.

cards.text: The earth mourns and withers, and the world languishes and fades. Big title or no title, even the exalted of the earth waste away.

cards.question: Isaiah says the earth is defiled by its people. They have transgressed the laws and overstepped the decrees. What else have they broken?
Isaiah says a curse has consumed the earth, and its people must bear the guilt. True or false: He says everyone on the earth survives.

cards.text: The earth's dwellers have been burned, and only a few survive. Then Isaiah turns to the vine.

cards.question: The new wine dries up and the vine withers. What happens to all the merrymakers?

cards.text: Tambourines, revelers, harp: all gone quiet, and friend, I KNOW that kind of quiet. Back when I was stuck in the back of a junk drawer, a rubber band snapping was the big news for a WEEK.

cards.question: The people no longer sing and drink wine. Strong drink is ___ to those who consume it.

cards.text: Then Isaiah turns to a city he calls the city of chaos. It's shattered, and every house is closed to entry.

cards.question: In the streets, they cry out for wine. All joy turns to ___.
True or false: When the city is left in ruins, its gate is reduced to rubble.

cards.text: Isaiah says it will be like this on the earth and among the nations. Then he reaches for a picture from harvest time.

cards.question: Isaiah says it will be like this on the earth and among the nations. He pictures two things from harvest time. What are they?

answers.text: A harvested olive tree and leftover grapes
A threshing floor and a winepress
A fig tree and a barley field

cards.text: Then the sound changes, baker, and voices go up, shouting for joy. From the west, they proclaim the majesty of the LORD.

cards.question: True or false: The only praise for the LORD anyone hears is coming from the west.

cards.text: There's a call to glorify the LORD in the east and in the islands of the sea, and from the ends of the earth there's singing: "Glory to the Righteous One." It's the world's biggest group chat, and for once EVERYBODY replies.

cards.question: The ends of the earth are singing glory to the Righteous One. Then the prophet cuts in with a but. How does he react?

answers.text: With a song of his own

cards.text: The prophet says, "I am wasting away! I am wasting away! Woe is me." Then: "The treacherous betray; the treacherous deal in treachery."
Then the message turns to whoever lives on the earth. Terror and pit and snare are waiting.

cards.question: Someone on the earth flees the sound of panic. Where does Isaiah say they end up?

answers.text: They reach a city of refuge

cards.question: True or false: Whoever climbs out of the pit is finally safe.

cards.text: Isaiah says, "For the windows of heaven are open, and the foundations of the earth are shaken." The earth is broken apart, split open and shaken violently.

cards.question: The earth is breaking apart and shaking violently. Isaiah says it staggers like what?
The earth staggers like a drunkard and sways like a shack. Earth's ___ weighs it down, and it falls, never to rise again.

cards.text: Then Isaiah speaks of that day, and what the LORD will do up above and down below.

cards.question: In that day the LORD will punish the host of ___ above and the kings of the ___ below.

cards.text: The host of heaven and the kings of the earth will be gathered together like prisoners in a pit, confined to a dungeon and punished after many days. And I thought the junk drawer I got stuck in for years was a tight squeeze.

cards.question: Isaiah says the moon will be confounded and the sun will be ashamed. Why?

answers.text: The LORD of Hosts will reign

cards.question: True or false: Isaiah says the LORD of Hosts will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem.

cards.text: He'll reign there before His elders, with great glory. And THAT, friend, is where this whole message lands.
